print.notes: Both runs mis-transcribed the diagram's own section labels as lettered ('Section A'/'Overlapping Section B'/'Section C') when the agreed braille uses NUMBERS ('#a'/'#b'/'#c' = 1/2/3, confirmed by forward translation — 'Section 1' reproduces ',sec;n #a' exactly, 'Section A' would instead give ',sec;n ,a' with no number sign). Both runs also placed the 'Division of...' heading BEFORE the 'Critical Thinking' box; the agreed braille places the Critical-Thinking box content FIRST (matching the book's own print layout note: the box sits at the bottom right of the diagram, transcribed at the point of encounter) — reordered here. Each section's own bullet ('_4' in the agreed braille) is Emboss's ordinary supported bullet, '•' (BANA 8.6.2a), confirmed by forward translation. Every one of the three sections' own bulleted lists is longer in print (figure.labels) than what this braille excerpt actually transcribes (each ends with the book's own ellipsis, 444, after 2-3 items) — not built, matching the excerpt-truncation convention used throughout this gold corpus. Two small elements are not modelled at all: the right-margin page-reference tokens trailing the 'Critical Thinking' and 'Section 3' lines ('b#ig'/'c#ig'), and the inter-braille-page continuation marker '#,-' on the line before the page break — Emboss has no construct for either (page-numbering/cross-reference mechanics outside this schema's scope).

braille.notes: The book's own text extract marks a real braille-page turn between 'Borrow money' and 'Section 3' (source-6.txt's own '—New Braille Page—' annotation, itself an extraction artifact, not braille content — recorded here as pageBreaks:[25] instead). Every bulleted item is at 3-5 margins (cell 3 first, cell 5 runover) under its own flush ALL-CAPS category paragraph.

resolution: CORRECTION (session-wide): the gold-6-A/gold-6-B braille arrays were produced by a script that wrongly blanked every all-digit braille line (it treated a line of only '4's or '7's as empty) — this cost both runs their '444' excerpt-ellipsis markers throughout this file (five of them: after 'Coin money', after the federal-courts item, after 'Borrow money', and after the two final items) and is the majority of this file's own reconciliation work; every one was restored by decoding source-6.txt directly (lines 5210-5240), not by trusting either run's blanked array. Beyond that restoration: both runs mis-transcribe the numbered section labels as lettered (Section A/B/C instead of 1/2/3, confirmed by forward translation) and reverse the Critical-Thinking-box/main-heading order relative to the agreed braille. print.blocks (the note/paragraph/list structure for each of the three sections) was built from scratch, since neither run supplied one, only a flat, unordered figure.labels array with no section grouping at all.
